title: SELLING A DIGITAL ONE-OFF: MINE OR SOMEONE ELSE'S?
content:
There are two very different ways to build around a digital product. You can own the product you're selling, or you can earn money from a digital product someone else owns.

Owning the product does not mean you must personally do every piece of writing, design, coding, or production. It means the offer is yours to control. Selling someone else's product means your rights and economics depend on another creator, company, program, or license.

That difference affects how much you need to create, how much control you have, what you can change, how you get paid, and what happens if the other company changes its terms.

IF IT IS MINE
You decide what the product is, who it is for, what it includes, and how it changes. You can hire people or use tools to help create it. Ownership is about control, not doing every task personally.

IF IT BELONGS TO SOMEONE ELSE
You can skip much of the original creation work, but you inherit constraints. Programs change, licenses restrict use, products disappear, and companies change prices or terms.

The question is whether you would rather take on creation in exchange for control or accept more dependence in exchange for starting with something that already exists.

DECISION CHECK
Choose MINE if the appeal is creating an asset your business controls and you are willing to take responsibility for deciding what that asset should be.

Choose SOMEONE ELSE'S if the appeal is starting with a product that already exists and you are comfortable building around another party's product, program, or license.

If your real answer is, "I want someone else to make it, but I still want it to be my product," that can still belong under MINE. Outsourcing creation is not the same as selling someone else's product.

I WANT THE DIGITAL PRODUCT TO BE MINE → PDF 06.
I'D RATHER START WITH A DIGITAL PRODUCT THAT ALREADY EXISTS → PDF 08.

WHAT CHANGES WHEN THE DIGITAL PRODUCT IS YOURS

If you create a guide, template, course, asset, or tool, the customer is buying an offer you control. You decide what problem it solves, what it contains, how it is positioned, and how it evolves.

That control creates creation work. You have to decide what should exist and make sure it is useful enough to buy.

If you sell an existing digital product, much of that creation work has already happened. Your question becomes what relationship gives you permission to participate in the sale and what you actually control under that relationship.

For example, an affiliate may have almost no control over the product itself. Someone with broad PLR rights may be allowed to edit and rebrand substantial portions of the material. A reseller may have permission to sell a product while having little permission to change it.

So "mine or someone else's?" is not really about whose computer produced the original file. It is about whether you are building the asset customers buy or entering an arrangement around an asset that already exists.

A SIMPLE OWNERSHIP TEST

Ask: "If this digital product disappeared tomorrow, would I be responsible for rebuilding the thing the customer buys?"

If yes, you are probably thinking about creating your own digital product.

If no because another creator or company owns the underlying product and your role is to refer, resell, license, or otherwise participate in its sale, you are probably in the existing-product branch.

This test is not legally definitive. It is simply a useful way to identify which problem you are trying to solve next.

WHERE TO GO NEXT
If you want control over the digital product itself, continue to PDF 06. If you prefer to work with a product that already exists, continue to PDF 08.
